---
# "By the numbers" state report: a state cover page followed by a two-page
# profile for every county in the state.
#
# `state` below is the report parameter. typst-show.typ passes it into the
# report() template (footer branding) and the setup chunk passes it to
# R/data-viz.R (data filtering). Render every state with R/render-reports.R, or
# one state with:  quarto render report/report.qmd -M state:Oregon
#
# Optional `county` override: setting it (e.g. -M county:"Los Angeles", bare
# name, no " County") renders just that one county's two pages, the old
# single-county report. Left unset, the full state report is produced.
#
# All Typst definitions live in typst-template.typ; this document only calls
# them.
state: California
format:
  typst:
    template-partials:
      - typst-show.typ
      - typst-template.typ
    keep-typ: true
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# Quarto executes this document from report/, where the repo root's .Rprofile
# does not run, so activate the renv library explicitly.
Sys.setenv(RENV_PROJECT = normalizePath(".."))
source("../renv/activate.R")

# The report parameters. R/render-reports.R sets BTN_STATE (and optionally
# BTN_COUNTY) per render; when unset, the YAML `state` above is the default.
# Environment variables are used rather than `-M`/metadata because knitr reads
# the YAML front matter before Quarto applies metadata overrides, so `-M` would
# not reach this R code (it would only reach pandoc and the Typst footer).
env_state <- Sys.getenv("BTN_STATE", unset = "")
focus_state <- if (nzchar(env_state)) env_state else rmarkdown::metadata$state
# Optional single-county override; "" (unset) means "the whole state".
env_county <- Sys.getenv("BTN_COUNTY", unset = "")
focus_county <- if (nzchar(env_county)) env_county else NULL

# All figures and report data come from the shared data-viz script.
source(here::here("R", "data-viz.R"))

# The state theme handed to the Typst layout: the accent color and its tint (so
# each state's report is a different color), plus the state name for the footer.
# Written before Typst compiles; typst-template.typ imports it. This keeps the
# accent defined once (data_raw/state_colors.csv, read by data-viz.R) rather than
# duplicated across R and Typst, and keeps the footer in step with focus_state.
writeLines(
  c(
    sprintf('#let focus-color = rgb("%s")', focus_color),
    sprintf('#let focus-fill = rgb("%s")', focus_fill),
    sprintf('#let report-state = "%s"', focus_state)
  ),
  here::here("report", "_state-theme.typ")
)

# Emit a raw Typst block from an asis chunk.
typst <- function(...) {
  cat("\n```{=typst}\n", ..., "\n```\n", sep = "")
}

# glue with << >> delimiters so Typst's own braces pass through untouched.
# .envir forwards the caller's environment so this works inside mutate().
tglue <- function(..., .envir = parent.frame()) {
  str_glue(..., .open = "<<", .close = ">>", .envir = .envir)
}

# ACS vintage, read from the import script so the sources note stays in sync.
acs_year <- read_lines(here::here("R", "import-data.R")) |>
  str_subset("^acs_year <-") |>
  str_extract("\\d{4}") |>
  as.integer()
acs_range <- str_glue("{acs_year - 4}–{acs_year}")
generated_date <- str_squish(format(Sys.Date(), "%B %e, %Y"))

# Export the figures the Typst layout embeds. SVG via svglite (named explicitly
# so renv::snapshot() keeps it in the lockfile). Figures are geoid-prefixed so
# the counties in one render do not clobber each other.
fig_dir <- here::here("report", "figures")
dir.create(fig_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
save_svg <- function(name, plot, width, height) {
  ggsave(
    file.path(fig_dir, name),
    plot,
    device = svglite::svglite,
    width = width,
    height = height
  )
}

# The locator map is rasterized to PNG instead of SVG: it embeds the state's full
# boundary geometry, which as vector paths repeats megabytes of coastline once
# per county (a 254-county state ran ~23 MB, near Cloudflare's 25 MiB/file cap).
# A small PNG is a few KB and looks identical at the 2.2in display size. The
# text-bearing charts stay SVG so their labels stay crisp.
save_png <- function(name, plot, width, height, dpi = 300) {
  ggsave(
    file.path(fig_dir, name),
    plot,
    device = ragg::agg_png,
    width = width,
    height = height,
    dpi = dpi
  )
}

# The county population table: n_table_cols side-by-side county/population pairs
# separated by spacer columns, filled top to bottom, left to right
# (population-table() in typst-template.typ builds the matching columns). Typst
# tables are a flat cell stream, so short columns are padded with empty cells to
# keep later rows aligned. Three columns is the most that fits the 5.8in content
# width without wrapping names; the " County" suffix is dropped so names stay on
# one line (the column header already says "County"). Pass a focus_geoid to bold
# and accent that county (single-county mode); NULL leaves the table unhighlighted
# (the shared ranking section in a state report).
population_table_typst <- function(focus_geoid = NULL) {
  n_table_cols <- 3
  rows_per_col <- ceiling(n_counties / n_table_cols)

  county_cells <- population_by_county |>
    mutate(
      is_focus = if (is.null(focus_geoid)) FALSE else geoid == focus_geoid,
      name = str_remove(county, " County$"),
      cell = tglue(
        '..county-cell("<<name>>", "<<scales::comma(total_population)>>", focus: <<tolower(is_focus)>>),'
      ),
      col = (row_number() - 1) %/% rows_per_col,
      slot = (row_number() - 1) %% rows_per_col
    )

  table_rows <- map_chr(seq_len(rows_per_col) - 1, function(s) {
    pairs <- map_chr(seq_len(n_table_cols) - 1, function(cl) {
      cell <- county_cells |> filter(col == cl, slot == s) |> pull(cell)
      if (length(cell) == 1) cell else "[], [],"
    })
    paste(pairs, collapse = " [],\n  ")
  })

  tglue(
    '#population-table(\n  <<n_table_cols>>,\n  <<paste(table_rows, collapse = "\n  ")>>\n)'
  )
}

# The shared "Counties by Population" section: the full ranked table, rendered
# once after the cover page in a state report (rather than repeated on every
# county page). Ends with the sources note and a page break.
emit_population_section <- function() {
  typst(tglue(
    '
#section-title(
  [Counties by Population],
  subtitle: [All <<n_counties>> <<focus_state>> counties, ordered from most to least populous],
)

<<population_table_typst()>>

#v(1fr)
#sources-note("<<acs_range>>", "<<generated_date>>")

#pagebreak()
'
  ))
}

# Emit one county's profile: the big numbers and locator map, then the
# race/ethnicity and income comparison charts. In a state report this is a single
# page (include_table = FALSE); the ranked county table lives in its own section
# (emit_population_section). In single-county mode (include_table = TRUE) it keeps
# the old two-page layout, with the full state table flagged to this county on
# page 1 and its own sources note.
emit_county <- function(focus_geoid, include_table = FALSE) {
  save_png(
    sprintf("%s-map.png", focus_geoid),
    county_map(focus_geoid),
    2.4,
    2.4
  )
  save_svg(
    sprintf("%s-race.svg", focus_geoid),
    race_plot(focus_geoid),
    5.8,
    2.9
  )
  save_svg(
    sprintf("%s-income.svg", focus_geoid),
    income_plot(focus_geoid),
    5.8,
    1.5
  )

  s <- county_stats(focus_geoid)

  # In single-county mode, the full state table (flagged to this county) plus a
  # page break sit between the stats and the charts, exactly as before.
  table_block <- if (include_table) {
    tglue(
      '
#section-title(
  [Total Population],
  subtitle: [Every <<focus_state>> county, ordered from most to least populous; #hl("<<s$label>>") highlighted],
)

<<population_table_typst(focus_geoid)>>

#pagebreak()
'
    )
  } else {
    ""
  }

  sources_block <- if (include_table) {
    tglue('\n#v(1fr)\n#sources-note("<<acs_range>>", "<<generated_date>>")')
  } else {
    ""
  }

  typst(tglue(
    '
#county-header("<<s$label>>")

#grid(
  columns: (1fr, 2.2in),
  column-gutter: 0.4in,
  align: horizon,
  [
    #stat("<<scales::comma(s$population)>>", "Total population")
    #v(0.25in)
    #stat("<<scales::dollar(s$income, accuracy = 1)>>", "Median household income")
  ],
  image("figures/<<focus_geoid>>-map.png", width: 100%),
)
<<table_block>>
#section-title(
  [Population by Race/Ethnicity],
  subtitle: [Share of total population in #hl("<<s$label>>") and #hl-gray("<<focus_state>>") as a whole],
)

#image("figures/<<focus_geoid>>-race.svg", width: 100%)

#section-title(
  [Median Household Income],
  subtitle: [#hl("<<s$label>>") among #hl-gray("all <<n_counties>> <<focus_state>> counties"); dots are spread vertically only to avoid overlap],
)

#image("figures/<<focus_geoid>>-income.svg", width: 100%)
<<sources_block>>
'
  ))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: report-body
#| output: asis

if (is.null(focus_county)) {
  # Full state report: cover page, the ranked county table once, then a
  # single-page profile for each county in alphabetical order.
  flag_rel <- sprintf("flags/%s.svg", state_slug)
  typst(tglue(
    '#state-cover("<<focus_state>>", "<<flag_rel>>", "<<scales::comma(state_total_population)>>", "<<n_counties>>")\n#pagebreak()'
  ))

  emit_population_section()

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(counties_alpha))) {
    if (i > 1) {
      typst("#pagebreak()")
    }
    emit_county(counties_alpha$geoid[[i]])
  }
} else {
  # Single-county override: the state band, then that county's two-page spread
  # with the full ranked table (the original single-county report).
  focus_geoid <- population_by_county |>
    mutate(bare = str_remove(county, " County$")) |>
    filter(bare == focus_county) |>
    pull(geoid)
  if (length(focus_geoid) != 1) {
    stop("County not found in ", focus_state, ": ", focus_county)
  }
  typst(tglue('#state-band("<<focus_state>>")\n#v(0.25in)'))
  emit_county(focus_geoid, include_table = TRUE)
}
```
